content.title: About
content.content: Fuji apples are a sweet apple variety developed in Japan in the early 20th century by crossing Red Delicious and Ralls Janet (Royal Gala). They are known for their crisp texture, juiciness, and balanced sweet‑tart flavor. Fuji apples are commonly eaten raw with the skin and are also used in baking, salads, and juices.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Fuji is one of the most popular apple varieties worldwide because of its taste and long shelf life.
Fuji apples can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 6 months without quality loss.
The skin of Fuji apples is rich in antioxidants, so it is recommended to keep it on when eating.
The name Fuji comes from Mount Fuji, a symbol of Japan.
Fuji apples are frequently featured in culinary competitions for their attractive appearance.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber improves digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Fuji apples are suitable for weight‑management diets because they provide volume with few calories.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: The skin and flesh contain quercetin and other polyphenols that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Fiber and potassium help lower cholesterol and maintain healthy blood pressure.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to apples, especially if they are sensitized to pollen.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Non‑organic apples may have pesticide residues on the skin; thorough washing is recommended.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: People with high stomach acidity may experience discomfort if they consume large amounts of apples.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fuji apples are typically eaten raw after rinsing under running water. The skin can be left on, as it holds most of the nutrients. They are great sliced into salads, added to oatmeal or yogurt, and used for compotes and baking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store Fuji apples in the refrigerator’s fruit drawer, preferably in a perforated plastic bag. At room temperature they keep for 1–2 weeks, but a cool environment extends freshness.
